inputs.question: What operation is exercised?
inputs.answer: np.core.records.fromarrays with 4000 arrays of length 5 and 4000 explicit field names, repeated 30x per timing sample

unknowns.subject: Relative cost of find_duplicate versus dtype construction and the per-field assignment loop

known: find_duplicate does a list slice plus an 'in' scan for every element
fromarrays runs a Python loop of one field assignment per array
unknown: Share of total time spent in find_duplicate
assumed: Field count is large, as in the workload (4000)
derived: With n=4000 names, find_duplicate performs at most n(n-1)/2 = 7,998,000 element comparisons and copies the same number of slice elements (derived from the loop structure)

root_causes.description: Duplicate-name detection uses an O(n^2) slice-and-scan instead of a hash-based check

findings.problem: find_duplicate, called by format_parser._setfieldnames from fromarrays, is quadratic in the number of field names: for each name it copies the tail of the list (list[i+1:]) and linearly scans it.
findings.performance_principle: Membership and uniqueness checks over a collection should use hashing (O(n)), not repeated linear scans, and should not allocate a copy per iteration.

evidence.statement: find_duplicate loops over i and evaluates 'list[i] in list[i + 1:]', allocating a new slice and scanning it each iteration.
_setfieldnames calls find_duplicate(self._names) on every format_parser construction; fromarrays constructs format_parser whenever dtype is None.
Derived: for n=4000 names (workload.py N), no-duplicate case does n(n-1)/2 = 7,998,000 comparisons and as many slice-element copies per fromarrays call. No runtime measurement is available.

findings.conditions: Matters when fromarrays/format_parser is given many fields (thousands, as in the workload). With a handful of fields the cost is negligible.

counter_evidence.statement: Other per-field work in fromarrays (asarray, formats join, per-field validation, per-field setitem on recarray) is O(n) in Python calls; it may have a large constant, so quadratic share is not measured.
Names are strings, so 'in' comparisons are fast C-level identity/equality checks; the constant is small but 8M of them plus slice copies is still substantial.

findings.why_this_might_not_matter: Real record arrays rarely have thousands of fields; the cost only dominates at extreme widths, and the per-field Python loops may rival it.
findings.recommendation: Replace the nested scan with a single pass using a set (or collections.Counter) that records seen names and collects duplicates in first-seen order, preserving the returned list semantics.

alternatives.option: Compare len(set(names)) to len(names) and only compute the duplicate list on mismatch
alternatives.why: Equivalent complexity; a single pass with a seen set is just as simple and always yields the list.
O(n), no slice copies, identical output.

findings.trade_offs: Uses O(n) extra memory for the set; names must be hashable (they are strings or coerced strings here).

validation.metric: Wall time of np.core.records.fromarrays with 4000 arrays and 4000 names, and cProfile cumulative time of find_duplicate
validation.expectation: find_duplicate time falls from quadratic to linear in field count; overall call time decreases by that share.
validation.falsifier: If a profile shows find_duplicate is a small fraction of fromarrays time at n=4000, the finding is not material.

commands.command: python -c "import cProfile,numpy as np; a=[np.arange(5)]*4000; n=['field_%d'%i for i in range(4000)]; cProfile.run('np.core.records.fromarrays(a,names=n)',sort='cumtime')"
commands.purpose: Profile to attribute time to find_duplicate versus the rest

considered_not_reported.observation: fromarrays assigns fields one at a time via recarray.__setitem__/field lookup in a Python loop (records.py:631), and builds dtype from a joined format string.
considered_not_reported.why_discarded: Linear in field count; inherent to the design and without evidence it dominates. Worth revisiting after profiling.
considered_not_reported.revisit_when: A profile shows time outside find_duplicate dominating at large field counts.
